n001.reason: Fan-shaped expansion develops several lanes before expensive creatures arrive.
n001.concern: Power one is vulnerable; extra reach can outpace the power needed to retain it.

n002.reason: A second accessible predecessor makes the Grey Wolf and Dire Wolf chain less draw-dependent.
n002.concern: An evolution still needs its predecessor in play; owning two does not bypass that condition.

n003.reason: Forward, lateral and backward influence gives flexible opening development.
n003.concern: Two efficient rank-one bodies may encourage pure tempo over later evolutions.

n004.reason: Two-step forward reach offers a different route toward contested columns.
n004.concern: Low power and spread tokens can leave distant positions difficult to defend.

n005.reason: A second printed continuous support source makes formation-based play available.
n005.concern: Overlapping support can stack; loss of the supporting creature can reverse the apparent advantage.

n006.reason: Accessible one-shot weakening offers an early tactical response rather than only raw power.
n006.concern: Two separate placement effects can combine against small enemies; original activation limits remain.

n009.reason: Another low-requirement Caterpillar supports the Butterfly alternative.
n009.concern: A low-power predecessor and its evolution can be awkward when drawn in the wrong order.

n010.reason: Forward and vertical influence develops neighboring lanes with a simple body.
n010.concern: Broad coverage needs placement planning; duplicate bodies do not supply a finisher.

n013.reason: The rank-two Boar converts developed tokens into solid power and further expansion.
n013.concern: Two rank-two copies can be stranded if opening influence is badly positioned.

n027.reason: An additional intermediate evolution supports multiple Cub lineages and the later Dire Wolf.
n027.concern: It cannot enter an empty tile and must not be treated as an opening card.

m001.reason: A second rank-one predecessor supports the high-requirement Elder Dragon route.
m001.concern: The powerful evolution remains conditional and may be held until enough development exists.

m002.reason: Another accessible predecessor gives the Royal Griffin route a reliable foundation.
m002.concern: The evolution support bonus can compound with a dense formation; it is not a free placement.

m003.reason: A second Firebird enables the Phoenix alternative without adding another resurrection card.
m003.concern: Self-return still obeys evolution conditions, lineage limits and the existing resurrection safeguard.

m004.reason: Rapid low-requirement expansion opens a route for the larger mythical creatures.
m004.concern: Power one trades durability for reach; duplicate openings can overextend.

m005.reason: Its explicit rear-facing enhancement rewards understandable sequencing.
m005.concern: Repeated placement buffs can accumulate, but targets and per-instance limits remain unchanged.

m007.reason: Weakening immunity provides a sturdy alternative to fragile expansion openers.
m007.concern: Defensive bodies can slow token development; immunity is not universal protection.

m009.reason: A second forward weakening option gives beginners a readable contesting tool.
m009.concern: Stacked small reductions are efficient against low-power enemies but do not solve every defense.

m010.reason: Another predecessor supports the Nine-Tailed Fox control alternative.
m010.concern: Return-to-hand effects require correct orientation and a legal evolution; they can help an opponent replay a placement ability.

m013.reason: A useful rank-two body with an explicit enhancement links opening development to formation strength.
m013.concern: Needs developed tokens; repeated enhancement can concentrate too much investment in one lane.

m015.reason: Rank-two long-range influence and an alternate Royal Griffin predecessor widen construction choices.
m015.concern: Drawing several higher-requirement bodies before an opener remains a risk.

a001.reason: A second Wisp supports the low printed power of Arcane through efficient expansion.
a001.concern: It supplies access rather than combat power and is vulnerable if unsupported.

a002.reason: Another placement-draw Familiar makes elemental dependencies easier to assemble.
a002.concern: Cycling can be efficient; each physical instance retains its existing single placement trigger and the deck remains fifteen cards.

a003.reason: An accessible conditional body rewards having an established friendly formation.
a003.concern: Its condition includes itself but is not satisfied merely by owning more copies.

a004.reason: A second Frost Sprite combines early weakening with the Ice Elemental prerequisite.
a004.concern: Power one is fragile and repeated weakening must meet actual target geometry.

a005.reason: Another lateral weakening source also supports the Fire Elemental route.
a005.concern: The lateral target is easy to misread; it is not unrestricted removal.

a006.reason: A second simple predecessor helps assemble the Water Elemental support formation.
a006.concern: The base body is weak and evolution timing can temporarily reduce available formation options.

a007.reason: Another Earth Sprite supports the defensive Earth Elemental alternative.
a007.concern: The evolved immunity has a fortification condition; the extra copy does not supply that condition automatically.

a009.reason: A second continuous forward weakening source expresses Arcane control.
a009.concern: Overlapping auras can be strong and disappear with their actual sources; immunity and targeting rules still apply.

a014.reason: An extra rank-two placement reduction gives a useful developed-position payoff.
a014.concern: Several targets can be weakened at once; token requirements prevent it being a universal opener.

a015.reason: A second Crystal Elemental supports deliberate adjacent formations rather than stronger printed statistics.
a015.concern: Overlapping continuous enhancement is a principal duplicate balance concern and must be checked in human play.

u001.reason: Another Skeleton supplies the complete Warrior-to-Champion chain.
u001.concern: The chain consumes occupied predecessors; an evolution-heavy opening can still stall.

u002.reason: An accessible resilient body supports steady development before death-related payoffs.
u002.concern: Its exact printed resilience is conditional; duplicate ownership is not an unconditional combat bonus.

u003.reason: Another accessible spirit supports the Phantom route and an alternative to skeletal development.
u003.concern: The later overthrow effect needs its actual predecessor and legal orientation.

u004.reason: A second death-trigger body supports sacrifice sequencing with existing replacement cards.
u004.concern: Repeated death effects can combine; no new resurrection or trigger allowance is granted.

u005.reason: Another low-requirement body gives the death/sacrifice strategy early material.
u005.concern: Death payoffs require actual events; adding expendable creatures can reduce surviving board power.

u007.reason: An additional spirit predecessor supports Phantom construction without relying on one identity.
u007.concern: It is still a low-tier body and does not bypass the evolution requirement.

u009.reason: A second destruction-trigger weakening source provides a tactical sacrifice option.
u009.concern: Two death effects can combine against neighbors; careless sacrifices may lose board control.

u011.reason: Another destruction-draw source helps recover cards while using replacement strategies.
u011.concern: Drawing is not automatic value if the available board cannot play the resulting hand.

u015.reason: An extra Wight makes a developed-position payoff for actual friendly destruction available.
u015.concern: Its history-based bonus is bounded and can be weak without earlier losses.

u027.reason: An extra intermediate Skeleton evolution supports more than one lineage.
u027.concern: Generated Skeletons and later evolution remain subject to their existing limits and board-space requirements.

c001.reason: Another simple expansion/fortification opener starts the defensive formation.
c001.concern: Fortifying too early can leave insufficient forward development.

c002.reason: A second diagonal expansion body supports both reach and the Scorpion evolution.
c002.concern: Its two forward diagonals reward careful placement and can leave the center undeveloped.

c003.reason: Another direct expansion/fortification opener supports Iron Soldier construction.
c003.concern: Efficient repeated foundations can snowball a lane; printed values and copy limits remain unchanged.

c004.reason: A second multi-direction opening body offsets the Kindred's more static defenders.
c004.concern: Low power means reach must be defended by later creatures.

c005.reason: Another opening body can fortify an existing rear friendly position on placement.
c005.concern: The rear target must exist; it is not unrestricted reinforcement.

c006.reason: A second death-trigger token source supports the salvage/replacement alternative.
c006.concern: The token gift requires an actual destruction event and legal friendly targets.

c009.reason: Another mixed forward-development/vertical-fortification body reinforces formation choices.
c009.concern: Duplicated defensive patterns may stall progress if used without expansion support.

c011.reason: Another placement repair option helps recover an explicitly weakened friendly formation.
c011.concern: The printed target condition matters; without a weakened ally it is mainly a weak body.

c013.reason: An extra rank-two high-power foundation gives a clear midgame objective and Guardian predecessor.
c013.concern: Five printed power at rank two is an existing efficiency concern; duplicates may amplify it.

c027.reason: A second intermediate evolution supports two Soldier lineages without duplicating a top-tier finisher.
c027.concern: It still needs Tin Soldier in play and does not keep all predecessor passives active.
